item.title: Big 12 Conference taking executive action to fix officiating after 2 screwups at BYU games
item.description: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Big 12 Conference taking executive action to fix officiating after 2 screwups at BYU games appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Big 12 keeps having officiating mistakes. In the BYU win over Arizona State, another officiating mistake occurred, and the Big 12 conference was forced to admit another misstep . Now, the conference is doing a deeper look into its officiating , per Jon Wilner of KSL News. “Per source close to the Big 12: Executive meeting this week w anyone involved in officiating (on-field, replay booth, command center, etc). Entire operation will be evaluated. Conference has had issues with application of the rules/officiating mechanics 3 weeks in a row,” Wilner posted on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The first mistake came in the October 17 game between BYU and Notre Dame . Notre Dame was driving late in the fourth quarter, down four against BYU. A pass from CJ Carr fell incomplete, ending the game. Still, there should have been a second left on the clock, which would have allowed Notre Dame another chance for the game-winning touchdown. Then, on October 24, with UCF hosting, BYU officials enforced a ten-second run off at the end of regulation. The runoff was incorrectly applied, and UCF should have had a chance to win the game in regulation. The Knights would go on to win the game in overtime. This past week, BYU faced off against Arizona State. In the first quarter on a second-and-goal play from the one-yard line, Bear Bachmeier attempted to stretch into the end zone, but fumbled before crossing the goal line. The ball was recovered at the two-yard line by Sione Moa, who advanced the ball into the end zone for a touchdown. The ball should not have been allowed to be advanced, though, and the ball should have been awarded to BYU for a third-down attempt. While mistakes happen in officiating, three weeks in a row is something that needs to be reviewed. item.title: Kevin Durant names his all-time greatest NBA starting five
item.description: Photo by Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images Kevin Durant made some bold choices while picking his all-time starting five in the NBA The two-time NBA champion was on The Mount Rushmore podcast with Shaquille O’Neal and spoke about various things, including how the LA Lakers legend would fit in the current NBA. Currently playing in his 20th NBA season, Durant has all the laurels to be recognised as an all-time great. He is regarded by many as one of the greatest scorers in the game, and because of this, the 38-year-old decided to pick himself for his all-time starting lineup. “I’m going to go with LeBron at my point. Since you (Shaq) picked Kobe, I’m going Tracy McGrady at my two guard,” said Durant on The Mount Rushmore podcast. “I’m going to go three and I’m going KG (Kevin Garnett) at the four.” The discussion then came down to the centre position and there was some confusion as the initial rules dictated that Durant was not allowed to pick O’Neal in his lineup. However, Shaq then came up with a solution, which was a direct trade of the centres. This meant that KD’s starting lineup now had LeBron James, Tracy McGrady, himself, Kevin Garnett and Hakeem Olajuwon. Collectively, KD’s lineup had 72 All-Star appearances, which was one less than O’Neal’s list, as the four-time NBA champion had Magic Johnson, Kobe Bryant, Michael Jordan, Karl Malone and himself in his starting five. The rules were simple: each of them had to come up with a different lineup, which is what made the segment unique. The hosts Ari Emmanuel and Ben Persky also came up with their starting fives, with some unique additions. However, fans would definitely be more inclined towards what Durant and Shaq had in mind when it came to their starting lineup. item.title: Report: Liverpool have huge Szoboszlai decision to make
item.description: Report: Liverpool have huge Szoboszlai decision to make Dominik Szoboszlai Dilemma Gives Andoni Iraola a Defining Liverpool Call Liverpool have reached an intriguing stage of the season, and one of the biggest talking points centres on Dominik Szoboszlai. A player once viewed as central to the club’s leadership group and tactical future is now facing fresh scrutiny over his place in Andoni Iraola’s side. According to the Mail, the debate has intensified after a run of matches in which Liverpool appeared to carry greater balance without the Hungary international in the starting line-up. That discussion is not without substance. Szoboszlai’s early-season standing looked beyond doubt. He had impressed through pre-season, took on a more prominent leadership role, and marked Iraola’s first competitive fixture with a decisive late goal at Newcastle. At that point, he looked every inch a foundational figure for the new head coach. Since then, the picture has changed. Injury interrupted his rhythm, Liverpool continued to pick up wins, and his return has coincided with growing questions over structure, spacing and midfield chemistry. It is a debate that cuts to the heart of how Iraola wants this team to function. Photo: IMAGO Midfield Balance at Centre of Liverpool Debate The argument against Szoboszlai, as set out in the reportby The Mail, is largely tactical. Liverpool have looked more secure when Florian Wirtz has operated ahead of midfielders willing to hold shape and do the less glamorous work behind him. In that structure, Alexis Mac Allister has found freedom to influence games more naturally, while Trey Nyoni has offered calmness in deeper areas and helped the side control transitions. There is a logic to that view. If Szoboszlai and Wirtz drift into similar zones, Liverpool can become easier to counter. That matters greatly for an Iraola side expected to press aggressively and recover the ball in advanced areas. If the spacing behind the attack is not right, the whole framework can quickly look fragile. The mention of the Arsenal game is important. The suggestion is that Liverpool lost control when Nyoni went off and Szoboszlai came on, a switch that altered the midfield dynamic rather than simply changing personnel. It points to a possible issue of fit rather than form. Why Dominik Szoboszlai Remains Too Good to Ignore Yet it would be rash to reduce the conversation to a simple choice of balance over brilliance. Szoboszlai remains one of Liverpool’s most gifted players, and the report makes clear there is still significant faith internally in what he can become over the coming years. His qualities are obvious. He offers goals from midfield, carries a real threat from distance, contributes from set plays, and brings the sort of intensity modern elite sides demand. item.title: Shedeur Sanders in line to start Week 9 as Browns place Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol
item.description: Shedeur Sanders in line to start Week 9 as Browns place Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns have been starting Deshaun Watson at quarterback all season long, despite initial indications that he could get benched. But that was only if things were going south. Instead, the Browns are out to a strong 5-3 record. While they just lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8, the Browns are still in good shape to make a push for the playoffs. However, Wednesday morning after Week 8, leading up to Week 9, the Browns made a huge announcement . They are placing Watson in concussion protocol, which puts his Week 9 status in doubt. That means Shedeur Sanders might finally make his first start of the year for Cleveland in Week 9 when the Browns face off against the New Orleans Saints . Browns might start Shedeur Sanders in Week 9 after Deshaun Watson news "Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol," the Browns announced Wednesday. They also shared a lengthy comment that reveals why this news comes so far after their Week 8 matchup. Watson was cleared to return to the game in Week 8 and didn't present concussion symptoms after the game. However, "On Tuesday morning, he reported to the medical staff that he began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol." Despite initially coming out of the week with no issues, Watson's symptoms came about and now have him in question for Week 9 as the Browns placed him in the concussion protocol. He could still play this weekend against the Saints, but it's likely a long shot considering how late of an add he was to the concussion protocol. MORE : Ravens' 6 best QB options to replace injured Lamar Jackson, from Jacoby Brissett to Shedeur Sanders That means Sanders, currently the team's No. 2 quarterback, is most likely to start for Cleveland and Todd Monken in Week 9. Watson has gotten the bulk of the work this season, though Sanders has come into two games, including against the Steelers this past week, when he went two-for-two for two passing yards in a very brief relief appearance for Watson. After throwing for 1,400 yards on a 56.6 completion percentage with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions during his rookie season, Sanders lost the QB1 job to Watson in 2026. He hasn't had a chance to play this season, given how well the Browns have played. But now, with Watson in concussion protocol and not likely to suit up in Week 9 against the Saints, Sanders might finally be in line to make his first start of his second NFL season. It's a great matchup too, so this is a chance Sanders cannot squander. item.description: The Cleveland Browns fell 27-6 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, dropping to their third loss of the season. Deshaun Watson left the game briefly in the first quarter after a helmet-to-helmet hit from safety Jaquan Brisker, then passed his concussion evaluation and returned for Cleveland’s next series. Watson appeared to clear two more evaluations, one after the game and another Monday morning, without showing symptoms. item.title: Casey, Jansen and Timoney start against Argentina
item.description: Ireland resume their Nations Championship campaign against Argentina in Dublin on Friday night [Getty Images] Nick Timoney, Craig Casey and Sean Jansen will start for Ireland against Argentina in the Nations Championship on Friday night, with Jamison Gibson-Park and Josh van der Flier on the bench at Aviva Stadium. With captain Caelan Doris and two-tour British and Irish Lion Jack Conan missing through injury, Connacht's Jansen always seemed the most likely to fill in at number eight for head coach Andy Farrell. The 27-year-old made a try-scoring debut for Ireland against Japan in July and followed that with a cameo as a replacement against the All Blacks a week later. The selections of Casey and Timoney, however, were less expected. Influential scrum-half Gibson-Park has arguably been Ireland's best performer in recent seasons. The 34-year-old missed the start of Leinster's season with a groin injury but made his return in the win over Munster on 24 October. With only that game under his belt this season, he will start on the bench with Casey preferred to start at nine in a half-back partnership with fly-half Sam Prendergast, who has recovered from a wrist injury. Ulster back row Timoney, 31, previously struggled to regularly break into the side despite strong form for his province, but selection against Argentina means he will be involved in his ninth consecutive Test. Seven of those appearances, however, have been from the bench and his start on Friday night comes at the expense of former World Rugby player of the year Van der Flier. With Garry Ringrose ruled out because of a hamstring problem, the experienced Robbie Henshaw will wear the 13 jersey, forming a midfield partnership with Stuart McCloskey. Wing Mack Hansen, prop Andrew Porter and Ryan Baird all start, having not featured for Ireland since the defeat by South Africa in November 2025. All three missed the Six Nations and summer fixtures in the Nations Championship through injury. Hansen starts in the number 11 jersey in what is Ireland's first home game since James Lowe's departure from Irish rugby, with Robert Baloucoune keeping his spot on the right wing and Hugo Keenan selected at full-back. Baird is selected at blind-side flanker, joining Timoney and Jansen in the back row. Porter's return at loose-head will be a considerable boost for coach Farrell after recent windows were impact by injury problems at the position. He will pack down alongside hooker Dan Sheehan, who captains the side in Doris' absence, and tight-head Tadhg Furlong. Furlong is free to play after he was cleared by a disciplinary committee of grabbing Gavin Coombes in the groin last month. With Tadhg Beirne and Joe McCarthy selected as starting locks, James Ryan must make do with a place on the bench alongside Van der Flier and Gibson-Park. item.title: Afghanistan vs. Zimbabwe prediction, team news, pitch report and betting tips for 1st Test
item.description: Afghanistan and Zimbabwe meet in Sharjah on Thursday, November 5 (11.30 a.m. IST) for the first of two Tests, on a ground that has not staged the format in a decade. The last one, in 2016, ended with West Indies chasing 154 against Pakistan. Since then, Sharjah has hosted 76 men's white-ball games and earned a name for slow, low-bouncing pitches and a sluggish outfield, with temperatures above 36 degrees forecast. Zimbabwe are likely to give a debut to Antum Naqvi, the Belgian-born batter with six hundreds in 24 first-class matches. Brian Bennett captains because Richard Ngarava has a back problem, and Sikandar Raza is missing. Afghanistan are without Rashid Khan, Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran, so Rahmat Shah leads a side coming off a draw with Bangladesh in Abu Dhabi. MORE: Virat Kohli vs. Babar Azam: Who is the greatest? Afghanistan vs. Zimbabwe prediction: Who will win? Afghanistan and Zimbabwe have each won two of their five meetings, with one draw, so nothing in the history separates them. Sharjah is the real opponent here. The surface is slow, the bounce is low and the outfield is sluggish, so runs will be hard to come by and the spinners will matter more than the quicks. That helps Afghanistan, who have Qais Ahmed and Zia-ur-Rehman, and it also helps Zimbabwe if Graeme Cremer or Vincent Masekesa play. Zimbabwe's batting is full of experience but short of big names, with Raza missing and a debutant in Naqvi. Afghanistan lack Rashid Khan, Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran, yet Rahmat Shah and Hashmatullah Shahidi give them a steadier top order. Afghanistan are also more used to these conditions. item.description: The Detroit Tigers have an interesting decision to make regarding Zach McKinstry this offseason, and a trade idea involving the New York Yankees could give president of baseball operations Scott Harris something to think about. What if Detroit could turn its former All-Star utilityman into one of baseball’s most recognizable former top prospects? That’s the possibility raised by a recent proposal involving Yankees outfielder Jasson Domínguez , the 23-year-old switch-hitter once considered one of the brightest young talents in the game. It’s a deal that would carry considerable risk for both organizations. But with McKinstry coming off a disappointing offensive season and Detroit looking for ways to improve its lineup, the idea deserves a closer look. item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 20: Brandon Aiyuk #11 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up prior to the start of the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Levi's Stadium on October 20, 2024 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images In a turn of events, San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has hired new representation and is filing for reinstatement, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Aiyuk, who has been on the Reserve/Left Squad list all season, recently hired Drew Rosenhaus as his new agent this week, as he looks forward to returning to the football field for the first time in two years. “Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has turned in paperwork to be reinstated, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus,” Schefter tweeted. “Aiyuk, who is currently on San Francisco’s Reserve/Left Squad list, will be reporting to the 49ers’ training facility Friday afternoon, per Drew Rosenhaus.” “Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,” Rosenhaus said. This development speeds up San Francisco’s timeline with Aiyuk, as Schefter added that the 49ers now need to keep him (under his current contract), find a trade partner, or release him before Tuesday’s trade deadline. Aiyuk is finally turning things around after a bizarre offseason following his sitting out the entire 2025 campaign after the 49ers voided around $27 million worth of guarantees. He had hinted for much of the offseason that he would sign with the Washington Commanders, even flaunting their gear on social media, while publicly calling out Jayden Daniels. Washington ended up signing wide receiver Stefon Diggs before the season started, ruling out the need for Aiyuk. Following his erratic behavior this offseason, it’s unclear if there’d be any real suitors for Aiyuk this season, but he could have his options in front of him by next Tuesday’s trade deadline following his reinstatement filing.

item.title: Jalen Washington’s eligibility case set to move to Indiana

The former North Carolina Tar Heel and Vanderbilt Commodore committed to Tennessee back in the summer, but lost eligibility in August. He lost an appeal last month in the Tennessee Supreme Court. Barnes confirmed what has been talked about for the last few weeks. “We understand they are going to move him to the Indiana case, which has already been resolved for now,” Barnes said on Vol Network after Tennessee’s win over Wofford. “That’s where he’s from. That’s his home state. I would like to think that they see he has got a chance to make some earnings and they will rule in his favor.” The 6-10 power forward averaged 8.9 points and 5.6 rebounds last season for Vanderbilt. He’s seeking a fifth year of eligibility following the NCAA’s new five-for-five rule. Barnes has expressed a need for more depth in Tennessee’s frontcourt, and Washington clearly fits that bill. “He changes our team,” Rick Barnes said in September. “He changed our team once he came on campus. item.title: Diogo Dalot insists Man United's dramatic comeback against Roma can 'change season'
item.description: Diogo Dalot believes Manchester United 's dramatic Champions League comeback against Roma can change their season. United trailed by two goals at Old Trafford on Tuesday before winning a memorable European tie 3-2. Bruno Fernandes ' retaken penalty started the recovery, with a last-gasp Matheus Cunha brace and an even later red card completing a spectacular fightback by Michael Carrick 's side. Roma had raced into a deserved two-goal lead, and a United side in the midst of a nine-match winless run had looked set to see that sequence reach double figures. That barren spell includes poor Premier League performances, and the Red Devils' worst start to a league campaign since 1986 which has left them 17th, just above the relegation zone on goal difference. Reflecting on Tuesday’s win, Dalot said: "I think a really good second half. I think we came with the right attitude. Matheus Cunha scored twice to win the game for Man United (Reuters) "We did pretty much everything that we needed to do to turn the game on and it's moments like this, it's nights like this that can change momentum, and hopefully we can change ours. Not just the manager, everyone is under pressure. "When you don't win games for this football club, every moment, every person, everyone involved gets under pressure, and we felt it obviously, because we're not near good enough of what we should have done. “And, like I said, nights like this can change momentum, can change seasons, and I think this win is going to give us confidence for the next games.” Attention now turns to Aston Villa's visit to Old Trafford, where United will attempt to follow up the Roma turnaround by winning their second Premier League match of the season.
